checks: The three vertices sum to zero and are affinely independent, giving an interior centroid. Edge PR has positive y and x+y; edge PS crosses both other planes because their values change sign. For small ε the origin stays in the triangle P_εRS by barycentric continuity. Then P lies between the origin and P_ε, so the filled hull is that triangle.
Interpolating the y=0 intersections gives 1/3 and −(1+ε)/(3+ε), so the normalized length grows by (1+ε)/(3+ε)−1/3=2ε/[3(3+ε)].

Interpolating x+y=0 gives 1/5 and −(1+ε)/(4+ε). The slope factor √2 cancels the normal norm, giving old length 9/20 and increment (1+ε)/(4+ε)−1/4=3ε/[4(4+ε)]. A shave missing both unselected planes leaves these increments.

overlap.comparison: Its positive planar variation requires both adjacent supports to have the right strict signs. Here edge PS violates that requirement, so the example shows why inspecting only PR is insufficient.

readability: The proof and its scope are clear.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The triangle computes strict growth of both unselected central sections despite one favorable exposed face.
